assessment: Phase 1a closed today, and it is the first thing on the critical path to close since 2026-09-02. The 16:00 CDT build reads phase 1a at 100 with its tenth deliverable -- 'One full trading session of green beats', a kind: proof, the one that could only be earned by the market being open -- finally done, on thirteen intraday harvests out of thirteen expected with zero failures. That matters beyond the percentage: 1a was the only irreversible job on the board, the one whose misses are history that no longer exists, and it is now demonstrably running clean for a full session rather than merely scheduled. The critical path 1a -> 2 -> 3 -> 6 therefore advances to Phase 2 (market data, 75%, two deliverables wip), and Phase 2's note is already specific about what it wants first: Close_Price appears unadjusted for splits, so an adjustment path and a reconciliation test come before any benchmark number is quoted. What does NOT change is who can act. Nothing else moved this fire -- gate amber on the same three blockers for the twenty-first day, main still 1a05afa, ZoltarOne silent a seventeenth day, the inbox untouched for 13.8 days, and eight order files sitting in the clone with not one ORDER_RESULT among them. I deliberately issued no work order for Phase 2. The constraint on this build is not a missing order; it is that nothing consumes orders -- fleet/dispatch has never landed on main, so an executor that only reads main can never see one, and c-0014.1 and c-0015.1 have been waiting on Andrew for that call since 2026-09-11. Adding a fifth unconsumed order to a queue that has moved nothing in 12.6 days would inflate the board and hide the real blocker. The honest reading is that 1a's close raises the value of that one decision rather than creating new work: the machine just proved it can run a session unattended, and the only thing standing between that and Phase 2 is a merge only Andrew can make.

items.title: Phase 1a is closed on evidence - first critical-path phase to close since 2026-09-02
items.why: 1a is the phase the plan calls urgent because intraday history is destroyed continuously, and it is the only job on the board whose misses are irreversible. Its closing condition was deliberately not 'the script exists' but 'section 08 has shown one full trading session of green beats' -- a proof that can only be earned by a market session running unattended and clean. That happened today. Against the end goal this is the first hard input the rest of the chain depends on: every honest execution-timing number the charter asks for is computed over the archive 1a fills, so a 1a that is merely scheduled and a 1a that is proven are different foundations for criterion 1. It also retires, without anyone editing anything, the beat-strip 'miss' cell the last two fires published as an unresolved emitter artefact: this reading shows thirteen consecutive ok beats and no miss, which is what the artefact reading predicted.

items.title: Phase 1a reads 100% with every deliverable done while its own status field still says in_progress and completed_at is null
items.why: In the same record, phases[id=1a] carries pct 100 and ten of ten deliverables at done, and also status 'in_progress' with completed_at null and eta '2026-09-03'. Two halves of one record disagree, which is the failure this project keeps rediscovering in a friendlier costume -- a declared field outliving the evidence beside it. It is low-stakes today because the derived half is the true half, but it is the kind of drift that later gets read the other way round: a consumer that keys off status rather than pct will report 1a as open indefinitely, and a phase that never records completed_at cannot be used to date the start of Phase 2. The emitter is the worker's lane and this brain does not write it, so this is stated rather than repaired.
items.acceptance: Either phases[id=1a].status becomes 'done' with completed_at set to the date the tenth deliverable was earned, or the record documents why status and pct are independent and a consumer should key off one of them. Checkable in data/results/build_status.json by anyone who was not here.
